why: This is a setting-specific engineering activity sequence built around an adaptive-optics demonstrator, rather than a reusable instructional element or a named adoptable product.

Adaptive optics workbenches are a domain-specific implementation of hands-on learning in which learners physically operate a functioning optical system; the apparatus itself is not a distinct general instructional element.
This is a single adaptive-optics workbench activity sequence for specified learners, hardware, and content rather than a domain-general instructional pattern.

The AO Demonstrator activity is a domain-specific instance of hands-on learning in which learners directly manipulate and operate a real system; the apparatus itself is not a general instructional element.

rejected.verifier: The claim reports comparative ratings of specific lab activities, not evidence about hands-on learning as a practice.
